issues.body: `scan_bare_words` still reduces the preceding token to `prev: u8`, while `ends_operand` excludes `>`. For `FILTER(<http://ex/a><1&&FLTR(?o)&&?b>2)`, scanning the first IRI leaves `prev == '>'`; the following compact `<` is consequently classified as an IRIREF opener. Because its body remains IRIREF-legal through the later `>`, `iriref_end` skips over `FLTR` and no `FILTER` suggestion is emitted. This is the same major correctness finding as round 4, and none of the new tests exercises the exact IRI-operand counterexample.
issues.fix_hint: Track the preceding token's lexical kind, not only its final byte, so a completed IRI operand ending in `>` is distinguishable from the greater-than operator. Add a real-path regression using `FILTER(<http://ex/a><1&&FLTR(?o)&&?b>2)` that asserts `FLTR` suggests `FILTER`, while retaining coverage where a greater-than operator is followed by a genuine IRI.
issues.title: Completed IRI operand before compact less-than still hides diagnostics

verdict.summary: Round 5 is stagnant. The round-4 major correctness defect remains: IRIREF/operator disambiguation still records only the preceding token's final byte, and `ends_operand` deliberately excludes `>`. After scanning a completed IRI operand, the immediately following compact `<` is therefore treated as a new IRIREF opener. In the prior counterexample, that false IRIREF consumes through the later `>` and hides `FLTR`, so the promised diagnostic is absent. The added real-path tests still cover variables before compact `<`, not an IRI operand before compact `<`.
